playbook.intent: A sponsor funded a programme and, three releases in, nobody in the room can answer which of the funded needs actually shipped. The chain is closed when each business need runs forward without a break through requirement, design, acceptance criteria, test and release to a measured benefit, and the matrix is retired at project closure with every orphan either linked or formally written off.
playbook.scope: Continuous flow that runs from project start to closure. Establish, populate, audit, and retire a traceability matrix linking business need → requirement → design → AC → test → release → benefit. End state — at every release, sponsor sees evidence that what was funded is what shipped.

success-criteria.criterion: Every funded business need carries a forward link to at least one requirement, and no requirement exists that cannot point back to a need
Requirements pulled from the tracker keep a stable identifier that survives renaming, re-scoping and a change of board
Each in-scope design element is attached to the requirement it satisfies; design nobody can trace to a requirement is either justified in writing or dropped
Acceptance criteria exist for every in-scope requirement and are linked to the tests that exercise them
Requirements with no test behind them and tests with no requirement in front of them are listed by name with an owner, not left in the tail of the matrix
Release notes name the requirements each release closed, so the sponsor can compare funded against delivered without asking a person
At closure the matrix is archived beside a benefit reading per need, and anything funded but never delivered is recorded with the reason it was not
